evidence: rule_sets.py:882-894 wraps tomllib.loads and catches TOMLDecodeError (889) and RecursionError (891-894), the latter raising RuleSetFileError with the path. Local CPython 3.14 tomllib/_parser.py (/usr/lib/python3.14) has no nesting-depth limit: grep for RecursionError/depth/max nesting finds only the NestedDict 'nested' key helpers. Inline tables and arrays parse by pure-Python recursion (parse_value to parse_array/parse_inline_table), so depth 5000 exceeds the default recursion limit of 1000 and raises RecursionError. The test (test_row_rule_limits.py:146-156) uses depth 5000 and asserts RuleSetFileError with the path. Only 3.14 source was read. 3.11-3.13 were not read, but the tomllib parser is the same recursive design with no depth limit there. The test's assertion would also accept TOMLDecodeError, so it does not distinguish the two paths, but the claim about behavior holds.

Read src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:564-753. _exists builds one exp.Exists per call. OwnerViaRule (693-705): one _deeper, one _exists, no nested own rule. InheritRule (706-716): one _deeper wraps the single _exists; _own_rule(parent) and parent_rule are compiled inside that block, i.e. inside the EXISTS body, so their EXISTS nest at depth+1 as they really do. Linked ReferencedByRule (730-752): outer _deeper for the link EXISTS and an inner _deeper for the source EXISTS, which is built inside the link condition, so two levels. The link's own rule is compiled at the outer level only, which is inside the link EXISTS body. AnyOf/AllOf (689-692) and CompareRule/IsNull/IsNotNull call no _deeper and add only their children's EXISTS. _own_rule (661-663) has no _deeper. The depth counter is restored in the finally at 647-648, so siblings do not accumulate. The claim holds.

docs/external/rule-sets.md:197 says 'two string columns with incompatible collations make every query on that table fail with MySQL error 1267'. src/sqllens/rule_sets.py _Compiler._node (lines 706-752) builds each join as a plain exp.EQ between the two slot columns inside an EXISTS. It adds no COLLATE, CAST or BINARY. The condition is compiled once per table with a row rule (compile, line 650) and is part of the predicate applied to every read of that table. The adjacent doc text and the compiler show no query shape that skips it, including a column-only query or a read through a link or parent table. An EQ between two implicit-coercibility string columns with no common coercion raises error 1267 when MySQL resolves the statement. This does not depend on row contents, on a short-circuiting any_of, or on the EXISTS being evaluated. The wording says 'incompatible', so it does not claim that coercible pairs fail. A pair such as latin1 and utf8mb4 coerces and does not error, and the doc does not say it does. Absolute-claim input traced: a rule inside any_of whose join is never true for the user, or a query touching only unrelated columns. Both still compile the EXISTS into the statement, so both still hit 1267. No counterexample found. Limit: the 1267 behaviour comes from MySQL semantics, not from repository source, and I did not run it against a server.

In src/sqllens/rule_sets.py (head), load_rule_sets wraps read_bytes, decode and tomllib.loads(text) (lines 875-882) in a try.
